key_insight: SpatialBench shows that spatial foundation models are not inherently "all-round" — their performance fluctuates significantly across tasks, viewpoints, scene domains, input densities, and hardware constraints, exposing gaps in generalization and robustness.
problem_solved: Provides a holistic, standardized benchmark to evaluate how well spatial foundation models generalize and remain robust across diverse downstream tasks, arbitrary viewpoints, domain shifts, varying input densities, and real-world hardware limits.
method: Assemble a comprehensive benchmark suite spanning multiple downstream tasks (e.g., detection, segmentation, localization) and a wide range of scene domains, viewpoints, and input densities.
Define standardized evaluation protocols and robustness metrics that capture generalization, viewpoint sensitivity, density tolerance, and hardware/efficiency trade-offs.
Evaluate popular spatial foundation models as baselines to reveal systematic strengths and failure modes across the benchmark dimensions.
impact: Enables practitioners and researchers to reliably compare models' real-world readiness, prioritize robustness over narrow benchmarks, and make informed choices for deployment and model design under spatial and hardware constraints.
visual_elements: Radar chart comparing model performance across key axes: tasks, viewpoint robustness, domain transfer, density tolerance, and efficiency.
Task×Domain performance matrix (heatmap) showing where each model succeeds or fails.
Illustration sequence of viewpoint and density shifts with corresponding performance drops to highlight sensitivity.
Bar chart or scatterplot of accuracy vs. runtime/energy across different hardware targets to show deployment trade-offs.
paper_title: SpatialBench: Is Your Spatial Foundation Model an All-Round Player?
paper_authors: Haosong Peng, Hao Li, Jiaqi Chen, Yuhao Pan, Runmao Yao
